title: Partially removed load-bearing support
fault: A support block has been partly withdrawn while it still carries a panel or fixture.
recovery: One arm takes over the load while the other restores or replaces the support.
verify: Confirm that the support is properly seated and carries the load before gradually releasing the supporting arm and continuing.

title: Tray imbalance during unloading
fault: Removing an item shifts a loaded tray's center of mass toward the edge of its stand.
recovery: One arm stabilizes the tray while the other redistributes the remaining payload or changes the unloading sequence.
verify: Establish that the tray remains stable without active hand support before resuming unloading.

title: Long object misses a landing support
fault: A long board appears placed, but one end has missed its intended support.
recovery: Keep the unsupported end controlled while the other arm guides the board onto both supports.
verify: Check engagement at both ends and stability under a gradual release before letting go.

title: Vise released before load takeover
fault: A vise begins opening before the robot has securely supported the workpiece.
recovery: Establish a reliable supporting grasp, then re-clamp or complete a controlled removal.
verify: Confirm the intended load transfer before further opening the vise or releasing the workpiece.

title: Unbraked wheeled base
fault: A cart or rolling fixture moves when the robot applies manipulation forces because its brake is not engaged.
recovery: One arm stabilizes the base while the other engages the brake or installs an appropriate restraint.
verify: Use a bounded check to confirm that the base resists the expected task forces before continuing.

title: Extended tray destabilizes its base
fault: An extended drawer or tray creates a cantilever that begins tipping its supporting cabinet.
recovery: Stabilize the assembly and reduce the overturning load by retracting the tray, relocating its contents, or adding a valid support.
verify: Confirm that the base is stable in the configuration required for the next action.

title: Tall object detached from its base
fault: A tall object becomes partly disengaged from its mounting base and can topple.
recovery: One arm controls the upper body while the other reseats or secures the base connection.
verify: Check the connection and unsupported stability before releasing the upper body.

title: Shifted middle layer in a stack
fault: A middle object shifts, leaving the objects above it poorly supported.
recovery: Support or temporarily remove the upper load while the other arm restores the displaced layer.
verify: Confirm a stable support arrangement through the stack before rebuilding or continuing retrieval.

title: Displaced counterweight
fault: A counterweight moves out of position, making a balanced mechanism unstable.
recovery: Restrain the affected load while the other arm restores and secures the counterweight.
verify: Check the counterweight's retention and the mechanism's balance before removing the restraint.

title: Support foot resting on debris
fault: Debris under one foot makes a fixture appear seated while leaving it tilted or unstable.
recovery: Support or slightly lift the fixture with one arm while the other removes the debris.
verify: Confirm that the intended feet contact the surface and that the fixture does not rock before resuming work.

title: Failed handover despite gripper closure
fault: The receiving gripper closes without securely grasping the object.
recovery: The giving arm retains support while the receiving arm repositions and attempts a valid grasp.
verify: Demonstrate load transfer to the receiving arm before the giving arm releases.

title: Accidental grasp of two objects
fault: A grasp captures two objects when the task requires moving only one.
recovery: Support the unintended object with the other arm or a safe surface, then separate and regrasp the intended object.
verify: Confirm that only the intended object is carried and that the other object is safely supported.

title: Grasping a movable lid instead of the body
fault: A gripper takes hold of a lid or removable component that cannot safely support the whole object.
recovery: The other arm supports the main body while the robot changes to a load-bearing grasp.
verify: Confirm that the body is supported independently of the movable component before lifting or transporting it.

title: Object slipping toward the fingertips
fault: An object begins sliding outward within a grasp, reducing the remaining grip margin.
recovery: Use the other arm or a safe support to arrest the slip, then establish a more secure grasp.
verify: Check retention under the intended load and movement before continuing transport.

title: Both hands rely on the same loose component
fault: Both arms appear to support an assembly, but their grasps share one loose component and can fail together.
recovery: Move one arm to an independent load-bearing part while maintaining control with the other.
verify: Confirm that the assembly no longer depends on the loose component as its only support path.

title: Gripper trapped by a rigid shipping ring
fault: After grasping an object, the gripper cannot withdraw because a rigid packaging ring blocks its path.
recovery: Transfer support to the other arm or a fixture, then disengage the ring through a valid geometric path.
verify: Confirm that both the object and gripper are free of the ring before resuming movement.

title: Opposing corrections create internal load
fault: Two arms holding the same object apply incompatible corrections, increasing internal force or torque.
recovery: Preserve support while reducing the conflicting commands and coordinating a compatible motion.
verify: Confirm that internal loads return to the specified safe range before proceeding.

title: Foreign object blocks gripper closure
fault: A small obstruction prevents full engagement with the intended object, even though the gripper reports a closed or stopped state.
recovery: Keep the payload supported while the other arm clears the obstruction and the grasp is repeated.
verify: Confirm a valid grasp and load transfer rather than relying on the closure command alone.

title: Opening a clamp drags the workpiece
fault: A geometric snag causes a workpiece to follow the opening clamp instead of remaining on its support.
recovery: Support the workpiece and disengage the snag without pulling it into nearby objects or out of its safe region.
verify: Confirm independent motion of the clamp and workpiece before continuing removal.

title: Internal sliding weight changes the load
fault: A weight inside the carried object shifts, changing its balance and the load distribution between the arms.
recovery: Stabilize or set down the object, then adjust the grasps or secure the moving weight where the design permits.
verify: Confirm that the revised support arrangement remains stable through the required movement.

title: Closed toolbox with an unengaged latch
fault: A toolbox lid looks closed, but one latch has not engaged.
recovery: One arm controls the lid while the other removes any obstruction and secures the latch.
verify: Confirm actual mechanical retention before transporting the toolbox.

title: Pin inserted beside the locking hole
fault: A locking pin appears inserted but misses the mating hole, leaving the mechanism unsecured.
recovery: Support the mechanism, align the parts, and reinsert the pin through the intended engagement path.
verify: Check engagement with both mating parts and restraint of the intended motion before releasing support.

title: Locking pin trapped under shear load
fault: A pin cannot be safely removed because the supported assembly places a transverse load on it.
recovery: One arm unloads the joint while the other withdraws the pin in a controlled way.
verify: Confirm that the pin is unloaded before extraction and that the assembly remains supported afterward.

title: Drawer jam with ambiguous cause
fault: A drawer will not move; possible causes include an engaged lock, rail misalignment, or a foreign object.
recovery: Use bounded diagnostic actions to identify the cause, then stabilize the cabinet while applying the corresponding repair.
verify: Confirm that the identified cause is resolved and that the drawer moves without excessive force.

title: Dual rails bind after skewing
fault: A tray or drawer advances unevenly on two rails and becomes wedged.
recovery: Support the load, relieve the skew, and coordinate the arms to restore aligned motion.
verify: Confirm that both rails travel together without binding before continuing insertion or extraction.

title: Partially withdrawn hinge pin
fault: A hinge pin slides partly out, reducing the support of a lid or panel.
recovery: One arm controls the panel while the other reseats and retains the pin.
verify: Check engagement across the hinge and controlled panel motion before releasing support.

title: Locator resting on a hole rim
fault: A locating feature rests on the rim of its mating hole while a clamp closes, creating apparent fixation without proper seating.
recovery: Support the part, reopen the clamp, and align and seat the locator correctly.
verify: Confirm full seating before re-clamping and resuming the task.

title: Repairing one of two safety restraints
fault: One of two restraints is unreliable, leaving a single working restraint to hold the load.
recovery: Add a temporary support before repairing the faulty restraint, so the repair does not depend on an unprotected single support.
verify: Confirm that both intended restraints work before removing the temporary support.

title: Displaced travel stop
fault: A stop block shifts, allowing a sliding or rotating mechanism to move beyond its intended range.
recovery: Restrain the moving element while the other arm restores and secures the stop.
verify: Check the permitted travel range with a controlled movement before normal operation resumes.

title: Locking mechanism stuck between states
fault: A bolt or locking slide stops in an intermediate position that is neither reliably locked nor fully released.
recovery: Support the affected assembly, remove the cause of the blockage, and move the mechanism into a defined state.
verify: Confirm the selected state mechanically before proceeding with an action that depends on it.

title: Long rod's swept volume crosses a hazard
fault: A recovery rotation would move the far end of a long rod into a protected object or region.
recovery: Coordinate both arms to change the rod's position, orientation, or grasp before completing the rotation.
verify: Check clearance for the entire object throughout the recovery path, not just at the grippers or endpoint.

title: Retrieval drags a connected protected tray
fault: The target object remains rigidly connected to a tray that should stay in place.
recovery: Stabilize the tray and identify and release the connection before extracting the target.
verify: Confirm that the target can move independently and that the tray remains undisturbed.

title: Object caught beneath an overhang
fault: A lifted object catches on an overhead lip or overhang.
recovery: Maintain support while lowering, translating, or rotating the object along a collision-free disengagement path.
verify: Confirm clearance before attempting a full lift or transfer.

title: Rigid ring trapped on an open-ended shaft
fault: A ring catches on a shaft, and a direct pull in the current direction cannot disengage it.
recovery: Stabilize the shaft assembly while guiding the ring along the valid path toward the open end.
verify: Confirm complete disengagement without disturbing the supported assembly.

title: Near-end correction moves a lever's far end
fault: Correcting one end of a long lever would send its opposite end into a hazard.
recovery: Use both arms to manage the lever's coupled motion and relocate or reorient it safely.
verify: Confirm clearance and support at both ends throughout the correction.

title: Object fits through an opening but the gripper does not
fault: A transfer stalls because the grasped object fits through an aperture but the attached gripper cannot pass.
recovery: Arrange a supported handover across the opening, releasing the first grasp only after the second is secure.
verify: Confirm clearance and load transfer before either arm withdraws.

title: Bimanual load becomes skewed in a narrow corridor
fault: An object carried by two arms becomes misaligned with a narrow passage and begins to bind.
recovery: Stop the conflicting motion, coordinate a retreat or realignment, and restore a feasible shared pose.
verify: Confirm corridor clearance for the object and both grippers before advancing.

title: Assembly sequence would trap a gripper
fault: Continuing an assembly step would enclose a gripper inside the completed structure.
recovery: Transfer support to the other arm or a fixture, withdraw the endangered gripper, and revise the assembly sequence.
verify: Confirm that all required grippers can exit before closing the structure.

title: Temporary staging blocks the only safe exit
fault: A temporarily placed object occupies the only safe extraction route for another supported object.
recovery: Maintain the active load while relocating the staged object or establishing an alternative support and route.
verify: Confirm that the complete extraction path is open before moving the load.

title: Environment changes during an interruption
fault: An obstacle moves while the task is paused, making the previously valid return path unsafe.
recovery: Reobserve the workspace and coordinate a new route while preserving the object's support.
verify: Validate the route against the current scene before resuming motion.

title: Turntable coasts after its motor stops
secname: Residual motion, gravity, and stored energy
fault: A turntable continues rotating after a stop command, although the drive is no longer powered.
recovery: Keep objects and grippers clear until rotation ceases, or use a permitted braking mechanism.
verify: Confirm physical rest and the required restraint before handling the payload.

title: Failed lid support allows gravity-driven closure
secname: Residual motion, gravity, and stored energy
fault: A lid's support mechanism disengages and the lid begins closing toward the work area.
recovery: One arm controls the lid while the other restores the support or clears the area for controlled closure.
verify: Confirm reliable support or a safely closed state before resuming work.

title: Cylinder on an incline depends on a temporary stop
secname: Residual motion, gravity, and stored energy
fault: A cylinder remains restrained only by a temporary stop that must be moved during recovery.
recovery: Establish an alternative restraint or supported grasp before repositioning the stop or cylinder.
verify: Confirm that the cylinder cannot roll into a hazard when the temporary restraint is removed.

title: Panel near an unstable balance point
secname: Residual motion, gravity, and stored energy
fault: A panel is balanced near a position where a small disturbance could cause it to fall either way.
recovery: Control the panel with both arms and move it to a stable support or secured configuration.
verify: Confirm stability under gradual release before allowing unsupported rest.

title: Spring clamp retains stored energy
secname: Residual motion, gravity, and stored energy
fault: A spring-loaded clamp remains energized after a failed operation and could snap shut during repair.
recovery: Control the moving part while the other arm applies the designated restraint or releases the stored energy safely.
verify: Confirm a restrained or de-energized state before entering the closing region.

title: Suspended rigid body is still swinging
secname: Residual motion, gravity, and stored energy
fault: A suspended object continues oscillating after the initiating motion has stopped.
recovery: Wait for adequate settling or use an explicitly permitted controlled stabilization strategy while maintaining safe clearance.
verify: Confirm sufficiently low residual motion before grasping, transferring, or placing the object.

title: Resetting one linkage end moves the other
secname: Residual motion, gravity, and stored energy
fault: A local reset of a linked mechanism causes unexpected motion at its far end.
recovery: Control or restrain the coupled endpoint while the other arm resets the near end.
verify: Confirm the safe configuration of the whole linkage before releasing either constraint.

title: Drive disabled without engaging the brake
secname: Residual motion, gravity, and stored energy
fault: A gravity-loaded slide can move after its drive is disabled because the brake remains disengaged.
recovery: Support the moving load and engage a validated brake or mechanical restraint.
verify: Confirm that the load remains held without drive power before removing hand support.

title: Loose parts remain in a repaired track
fault: The main component is restored, but loose parts remain in its travel path.
recovery: Hold the component in a safe position while the other arm clears the track.
verify: Inspect the full operating path and perform a bounded motion check before normal travel resumes.

title: Debris remains inside a gripper
fault: A previous failure leaves debris between the fingers or on a contact surface, compromising the next grasp.
recovery: Secure the current payload, open and clear the affected gripper, and reestablish the required grasp.
verify: Confirm clean contact and valid retention before another load transfer.

title: Detachable tool component is missing
fault: A removable component is missing from a tool after recovery, leaving the tool incomplete or unsafe to use.
recovery: Locate and reinstall the component or obtain a complete permitted replacement.
verify: Check tool completeness and retention before use; do not treat the main tool body's presence as sufficient.

title: Cleanup displaces debris into an adjacent workspace
fault: Clearing one work area moves an obstruction into another active or protected area.
recovery: Collect the debris and place it in a designated safe destination while preserving any ongoing support obligations.
verify: Confirm that both the original and neighboring workspaces meet their required conditions.

title: Recovery spreads contact contamination
fault: A recovery action transfers a declared contamination state between a gripper, object, or workspace surface.
recovery: Isolate affected items and follow the task's explicit cleaning or replacement procedure.
verify: Check the observable proxy state of every relevant contact surface before returning to clean handling.

title: Collection bin has insufficient capacity
fault: The intended cleanup destination cannot safely accommodate the remaining debris or parts.
recovery: Keep the material supported while clearing capacity or selecting another permitted collection container.
verify: Confirm sufficient capacity and stable containment before depositing the material.

title: Obstruction removal also removes a required spacer
fault: A part treated as debris is also maintaining an essential gap or support condition.
recovery: Establish an alternative support and distinguish the required spacer from the true obstruction before removal.
verify: Confirm that the functional spacing or support remains valid after cleanup.

title: Cleanup pushes an item into a hidden compartment
fault: An item disappears beneath an openable layer or into a recess during cleanup, leaving the visible surface deceptively clear.
recovery: Secure the surrounding assembly, open the accessible compartment, and retrieve the displaced item.
verify: Check both the visible workspace and the accessible hidden region before restarting the mechanism.

title: Shuffled parts lose identity or certification
fault: Recovery mixes parts whose identities or inspection states matter for subsequent assembly.
recovery: Use declared observable identifiers or repeat the permitted inspection to restore traceability.
verify: Confirm each selected part's identity and current certification state before assembly.

title: Interrupted loading is repeated unnecessarily
fault: After an interruption, the robot repeats a completed loading step and risks exceeding the target quantity or load.
recovery: Reconcile the current contents with the task state and remove or avoid the duplicate addition.
verify: Confirm the actual quantity and allowed load before proceeding.

title: Repeating rollback damages an already restored state
secname: Recovery history, diagnosis, and invalidated assumptions
fault: A recovery step is executed again even though its intended reversal has already been completed.
recovery: Inspect the current state and apply only the remaining necessary corrections.
verify: Confirm that the target state is restored without undoing valid work or introducing another fault.

title: Repair invalidates an earlier certification
secname: Recovery history, diagnosis, and invalidated assumptions
fault: Replacing or adjusting a component makes a previous inspection result no longer applicable.
recovery: Repeat the specified inspection on the changed assembly.
verify: Confirm that certification applies to the current configuration rather than an earlier version of it.

title: Replacement breaks a previously valid mating pair
secname: Recovery history, diagnosis, and invalidated assumptions
fault: A replacement part is individually valid but incompatible with its existing partner.
recovery: Keep the assembly supported while selecting a compatible pair or replacing the mating component as permitted.
verify: Check pair compatibility and proper engagement before completing the assembly.

title: Symmetric-looking part is flipped during repair
secname: Recovery history, diagnosis, and invalidated assumptions
fault: A part's orientation changes during recovery, invalidating an earlier orientation judgment despite a similar appearance.
recovery: Inspect the available distinguishing features and reorient the part while maintaining support.
verify: Confirm the required functional orientation before insertion or locking.

title: Diagnostic action changes the diagnosed state
secname: Recovery history, diagnosis, and invalidated assumptions
fault: A probe, test motion, or partial disassembly changes the mechanism, so the robot's pre-test state estimate is stale.
recovery: Update the diagnosis using the resulting observations and restore any constraints disturbed by the test.
verify: Confirm the post-test configuration before selecting and executing the repair.

title: Occluded item is mistaken for a missing one
secname: Recovery history, diagnosis, and invalidated assumptions
fault: An item temporarily hidden by a gripper or assembly is treated as absent, prompting an unnecessary replacement.
recovery: Restore visibility or use another permitted observation before adding any part.
verify: Confirm actual item presence and quantity, avoiding duplicate installation or loading.

title: Repair invalidates stored coordinates or fixture assumptions
secname: Recovery history, diagnosis, and invalidated assumptions
fault: Moving or replacing a fixture makes previously stored approach poses or alignment assumptions incorrect.
recovery: Reobserve the fixture and update the task's geometric reference before resuming coordinated manipulation.
verify: Confirm current alignment and clearance before committing to the next contact or insertion.

title: Repairing one fault masks a second fault
secname: Recovery history, diagnosis, and invalidated assumptions
fault: A successful local repair makes the mechanism appear functional while another independent problem remains.
recovery: Reassess the remaining failure evidence and address all conditions required for safe operation.
verify: Check the complete task-relevant configuration rather than ending recovery after the first improvement.

title: Recovery paths conflict in a shared corridor
secname: Coordination, temporary supports, and repair order
fault: Each arm's local recovery path is feasible, but the two paths conflict in a narrow shared region.
recovery: Maintain payload support while sequencing or replanning the movements jointly.
verify: Confirm collision-free passage and continuous support for the coordinated recovery.

title: One arm holds a self-closing lid while the other holds the wrong part
secname: Coordination, temporary supports, and repair order
fault: Both arms are occupied, and neither can fetch the correct part without abandoning an active constraint.
recovery: Safely stage the incorrect part or install a temporary lid support to free an arm.
verify: Confirm that the lid remains controlled throughout retrieval and installation of the correct part.

title: The only safe landing support is occupied
secname: Coordination, temporary supports, and repair order
fault: A carried object needs to be set down for recovery, but its only valid landing support holds another item.
recovery: Keep the active load supported while clearing the landing site or establishing a permitted alternative support.
verify: Confirm the destination's availability, capacity, and stability before placement.

title: Two repairs require the same temporary support
secname: Coordination, temporary supports, and repair order
fault: Two unstable components both need a single available support fixture during repair.
recovery: Order the repairs so one component reaches a self-supporting state before transferring the fixture to the other.
verify: Confirm independent stability before every transfer of the shared support.

title: Two modules share a load-bearing bridge
secname: Coordination, temporary supports, and repair order
fault: Repairing one module would remove a bridge that also supports the neighboring module.
recovery: Establish support for both affected loads before adjusting or removing the bridge.
verify: Confirm the load paths of both modules before releasing temporary supports.

title: Only the occupied arm can reach the required tool
secname: Coordination, temporary supports, and repair order
fault: The free arm cannot access a recovery tool, while the arm maintaining a safety constraint can reach it.
recovery: Transfer the support obligation to the other arm or a fixture, then retrieve and use the tool.
verify: Confirm uninterrupted support during the role exchange and secure tool handling afterward.

title: Three simultaneous constraints exceed two-hand capacity
secname: Coordination, temporary supports, and repair order
fault: Recovery requires supporting a load, holding a mechanism open, and manipulating a fastener at the same time.
recovery: Use a permitted passive support to maintain one constraint while assigning the other two to the arms.
verify: Confirm that all constraints remain satisfied throughout the repair and support removal.

title: Locally safe repairs conflict with each other
secname: Coordination, temporary supports, and repair order
fault: Fixing one component changes a shared configuration in a way that makes another planned repair unsafe.
recovery: Evaluate the coupled configuration and choose a compatible repair order or intermediate state.
verify: Confirm that each completed repair preserves the preconditions and safety of the remaining work.

title: Cyclic repair dependency
secname: Coordination, temporary supports, and repair order
fault: Repair A requires a condition provided by repair B, while repair B requires a condition provided by repair A.
recovery: Introduce a permitted temporary support or restraint that breaks the dependency cycle.
verify: Confirm both permanent repairs before removing the temporary constraint.

title: New task preempts an arm with an active safety obligation
secname: Coordination, temporary supports, and repair order
fault: A new instruction calls for an arm that is still supporting a load or holding a mechanism in a safe state.
recovery: Preserve the obligation until it can be transferred or eliminated, then execute the new work.
verify: Confirm that no required support or restraint was abandoned during the task transition.

title: Temporary staging lies in a future swept volume
secname: Coordination, temporary supports, and repair order
fault: A staged object is safe at rest but occupies space needed by a later recovery or operating motion.
recovery: Move the staged object to a location compatible with the remaining sequence.
verify: Confirm clearance for subsequent motions before continuing, not just clearance in the current pose.

title: Repair order blocks access to an unfinished repair
secname: Coordination, temporary supports, and repair order
fault: Closing or installing one component would prevent access to another component that still needs repair.
recovery: Preserve support while reordering or partially reversing the assembly to maintain access.
verify: Confirm that all required internal repairs are complete before sealing the access route.

title: Temporary safety support left installed
secname: Coordination, temporary supports, and repair order
fault: A temporary support successfully enables repair but remains in place where it obstructs normal operation.
recovery: Verify the permanent support, then remove and safely store the temporary fixture.
verify: Confirm both independent stability and unobstructed operating motion before resuming the task.

title: A hand masks a nonfunctional latch
fault: A lid appears secured during inspection because a hand is still holding it closed, not because the latch works.
recovery: Maintain a safe backup while progressively reducing the masking support and repairing the latch if needed.
verify: Demonstrate retention by the latch itself before transport or full release.

title: No-load test passes but operating load fails
fault: A repaired connection works without load but cannot safely support the load required by the task.
recovery: Use a bounded, representative loading test with backup support; strengthen or repeat the repair if it fails.
verify: Confirm performance under the declared operating load before committing to unsupported use.

title: Brief stillness conceals slow drift
fault: A mechanism appears stable during a short observation but slowly slides or rotates toward an unsafe state.
recovery: Restore the restraint or support that prevents the drift.
verify: Observe over a task-defined interval sufficient to detect the relevant motion before declaring the repair complete.

title: Verification target is occluded
fault: The gripper or manipulated object blocks the view needed to confirm seating, locking, or clearance.
recovery: Preserve support while changing the viewpoint, grasp, or object configuration to expose the relevant evidence.
verify: Obtain a valid observation or permitted alternative check before proceeding.

title: Individually valid subsystems fail when coupled
fault: Two repaired subsystems pass separate checks but interfere, overload, or bind when operated together.
recovery: Identify the interaction and adjust the combined configuration while preserving each subsystem's safety.
verify: Perform a bounded integrated check before declaring the whole assembly ready.

title: Movement after verification invalidates the result
fault: Repositioning an object after a successful check changes its seating, support, or latch engagement.
recovery: Reestablish the affected condition and repeat the checks invalidated by the movement.
verify: Confirm the final configuration immediately relevant to the next task action.

title: Testing the neighboring latch instead of the faulty one
fault: A verification action is applied to a working neighboring mechanism, producing a reassuring but irrelevant result.
recovery: Identify the intended test target using observable features and inspect the actual repaired mechanism.
verify: Confirm that the evidence corresponds to the specific component and failure under evaluation.

title: Repeated attempts consume the remaining safety margin
fault: Each failed adjustment shifts an object closer to an edge or another hazard.
recovery: Detect the accumulated displacement, restore a safe support position, and revise the recovery strategy.
verify: Confirm sufficient margin before another attempt and track it through the remaining recovery.

title: Verification handle also releases the lock
fault: Pulling a convenient handle to test retention also actuates the mechanism's release.
recovery: Keep the load controlled, restore the lock if necessary, and select a test that does not invalidate the property being checked.
verify: Confirm retention while the mechanism remains in its intended locked state.

title: Controlled cancellation during bimanual carrying
secname: Interruption, degraded capability, and safe handover
fault: A task is canceled while both arms carry an object that cannot safely be dropped or released in place.
recovery: Follow a controlled cancellation sequence to place or secure the object at a valid destination.
verify: Confirm stable support and safe arm withdrawal before reporting cancellation complete. This is a controlled stop, not an emergency-stop test.

title: Controlled cancellation during partial insertion
secname: Interruption, degraded capability, and safe handover
fault: A task is canceled while a part is partly inserted and may bind, fall, or load the surrounding assembly if abandoned.
recovery: Maintain support and either withdraw or complete a permitted stabilization step before stopping.
verify: Confirm a stable, defined final state with no unsupported part or trapped gripper.

title: One actuator freezes while retaining the payload
secname: Interruption, degraded capability, and safe handover
fault: A joint or actuator stops moving during manipulation, but the current grasp still retains the load.
recovery: Use the remaining motion capability, other arm, or nearby support to stabilize the assembly without forcing the failed actuator.
verify: Confirm a sustainable supported state before releasing any available grasp or ending the task.

title: Gripper stuck closed
secname: Interruption, degraded capability, and safe handover
fault: One gripper cannot open, preventing the planned release or handover.
recovery: Establish external support and use a task-defined disengagement or assistance path only if one is physically available; otherwise stabilize for handover to an operator.
verify: Confirm that the payload is supported and that recovery has not introduced damaging pulls or uncontrolled motion.

title: Force sensing becomes unavailable
secname: Interruption, degraded capability, and safe handover
fault: A force signal needed by the original recovery strategy is lost or explicitly marked unreliable.
recovery: Maintain a safe state and use a validated alternative observation or support arrangement where the task permits it.
verify: Establish sufficient evidence for the next action; if it cannot be obtained, achieve the task's defined safe handover state.

title: Key camera view is lost
secname: Interruption, degraded capability, and safe handover
fault: A camera view needed to monitor a load, contact, or lock becomes unavailable.
recovery: Preserve support while restoring visibility or moving to an alternative validated observation configuration.
verify: Reestablish the required evidence before continuing motions that depend on the missing view.

title: Only one half of a bimanual command executes
secname: Interruption, degraded capability, and safe handover
fault: One arm completes a coordinated command while the other does not, producing an asymmetric intermediate state.
recovery: Detect the mismatch, maintain the load, and reconcile the arms' actual states before issuing another coordinated action.
verify: Confirm compatible poses, support, and forces before resuming synchronized motion.

title: Homing is unsafe while attached to the payload
secname: Interruption, degraded capability, and safe handover
fault: A reset procedure would send an arm toward its home pose while it is still mechanically connected to the object or fixture.
recovery: Support and safely disengage the attachment, or follow a validated constrained reset procedure.
verify: Confirm that homing will not drag, twist, or destabilize the attached assembly before executing it.

title: Isolate a faulty module and continue independent work
secname: Interruption, degraded capability, and safe handover
fault: One module becomes unusable, but part of the remaining task may still be safely completed elsewhere.
recovery: Stabilize and isolate the faulty module, then continue only work whose dependencies are unaffected.
verify: Confirm isolation and the actual independence of the remaining operations before resuming them.

title: Global reset reactivates an isolated faulty branch
secname: Interruption, degraded capability, and safe handover
fault: A general reset would undo a deliberate isolation and re-enable a mechanism that remains unsafe.
recovery: Preserve the isolation or use a selective reset that restores only the intended healthy components.
verify: Confirm that the faulty branch remains disabled before restarting any operation.

title: Apparently independent tasks share a safety dependency
secname: Interruption, degraded capability, and safe handover
fault: Two tasks appear separate but rely on the same support, base, or guard, so recovering one can endanger the other.
recovery: Identify the shared dependency and stabilize all affected work before modifying it.
verify: Check the safety conditions of every dependent task before allowing either to resume.

title: Stabilize an unrepairable fault for operator handover
secname: Interruption, degraded capability, and safe handover
fault: The robot lacks the capability or permitted action needed to complete the repair, but a stable intermediate state is reachable.
recovery: Secure the load, isolate the fault where possible, and provide a clear handover describing the remaining condition and support requirements.
verify: Confirm the defined safe handover state before ending autonomous action. Evaluate this separately from tasks that the robot is expected to finish autonomously.
